method: Each claim below cites a page that was opened and read. Sources with ids starting 'pa-' and no 'reviewed_on' here come from the October 24, 2026 research batch (data/research/pennsylvania-2026-10-24-sources.json) and keep that review date; they were not reread. Sources listed in this file were read on October 28, 2026. A source supports only the stated claim. No service is described as available, free or guaranteed unless its own page says so, and coverage is recorded only where the page names a state or county. Pathway coverage text is maintained in the canonical Pennsylvania state pack, which later reviewed additions also update, so this importer does not rewrite it.

clean-slate.limitations: Statute text of 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2. Whether a particular record qualifies depends on the full record, restitution and exclusions in the statute. Not legal advice.

rules.summary: Medical use is lawful only under the Medical Marijuana Act: a registered patient or caregiver with a Department of Health ID card and practitioner certification. A dispensary may not dispense more than a 90-day supply. Smoking medical marijuana is unlawful; patients and caregivers may make edibles themselves.

evidence.value: Section 304(b)(1) makes it unlawful to smoke medical marijuana; 304(c) allows patients or caregivers to incorporate it into edible form; Sections 405 and 801 limit receipt to a 90-day supply. The act took effect 30 days after April 17, 2016 (Section 2110).

rules.summary: Pennsylvania has no adult-use (recreational) cannabis law. Without a medical card, possessing up to 30 grams of marijuana or 8 grams of hashish for personal use is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 30 days in jail, a fine of up to $500, or both. Some cities have their own ordinances; this summary covers state law only.

evidence.value: 35 P.S. § 780-113(a)(31) defines a small amount as 30 grams of marihuana or 8 grams of hashish; § 780-113(g) sets imprisonment not exceeding thirty days, a fine not exceeding $500, or both. Section 13 took effect immediately on enactment (Section 44).
As of October 13, 2026, adult-use cannabis is not legal in Pennsylvania; House Bill 1200 passed the House and died in a Senate committee.

rules.summary: Home cultivation is not allowed. Only grower/processors permitted by the Department of Health may grow medical marijuana, and Pennsylvania has no adult-use home-grow law. Growing hemp requires a separate Department of Agriculture permit.

evidence.value: Section 304(b)(3) makes it unlawful to grow medical marijuana unless the grower/processor has received a permit from the department.

rules.summary: An employer may not fire, refuse to hire or otherwise discriminate against someone solely because they are certified to use medical marijuana. Employers need not allow use at work and may discipline employees for being under the influence at work when their conduct falls below the standard of care for the job.

evidence.value: Section 2103(b)(1)-(3): no discharge, refusal to hire or discrimination solely on certification status; no required accommodation of use on employer premises; discipline allowed for working under the influence; no act required that would violate federal law.

rules.summary: Driving with any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance or its metabolite in your blood is DUI, whether or not you are impaired. Marijuana is a Schedule I substance under Pennsylvania law, and the DUI statute has no exception for medical marijuana patients.

evidence.value: 75 Pa.C.S. § 3802(d)(1)(i) and (iii): any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance, or its metabolite, in the individual's blood. No subsection mentions medical marijuana. Source note lists amendments of May 11, 2006 and December 22, 2025 (Act 58, which changed subsections (g) and (h) only).
evidence.limitations: The effective date shown is the earliest date in the General Assembly's source note; the subsection may be older.

evidence.value: 35 P.S. § 780-104(1)(iv) lists marihuana in Schedule I.

rules.summary: Clean Slate limits access to (seals) certain records automatically: charges that did not end in a conviction; summary convictions after five years; and second- and third-degree misdemeanors and misdemeanors punishable by up to two years after seven years free of convictions punishable by a year or more. Court-ordered restitution must be paid. A pardon is a separate step.

evidence.value: 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122.2(a)(1)-(3) as amended by Act 36 of 2023 (Dec. 14, 2023, P.L.334), which took effect in 180 days for these subsections.
Act 36 took effect February 12, 2024, except automated sealing, which took effect June 11, 2024; misdemeanor waiting period 7 years (previously 10) and summary convictions 5 years.
